[[File:Iwa-jinja (Matsumoto) torii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]]
'''Iwa Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|伊和神社}}, ''Iwa-jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Matsumoto, Nagano|en|松本市}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|長野県}}, Japan. It is presumed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja}} of {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province}}. Its modern status is a former {{ill|Village Shrine|en|村社}}. The official name is "Iwa-sha," but it is commonly referred to as "Iwa Shrine."<ref>[http://www.nagano-jinjacho.jp/shibu/syouenchiku.htm 松塩筑支部] (Nagano Prefecture Shrine Bureau).</ref> 

=== Deities ===
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)<ref>[http://www.genbu.net/data/sinano/iwa_title.htm 伊和神社] (Genbuko personal website).</ref>

=== History ===
In ancient times, {{ill|provincial governors|en|国司}} visited all shrines in their provinces, starting from the {{ill|Ichinomiya|en|Ichinomiya}}. To facilitate this, a {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja}} was established near the provincial capital to enshrine the gods collectively for easier rituals. Iwa Shrine is presumed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja}} of {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province}}. 

The provincial capital was initially located near {{ill|Ueda, Nagano|en|Ueda, Nagano}}, but it is believed to have moved to {{ill|Matsumoto, Nagano|en|Matsumoto, Nagano}} in the early Heian period.<ref>"Shinano Province" in {{Cite book|title=Nagano Prefecture Place names|editor=平凡社}}.</ref> The area around the shrine has been called "Sōja" since ancient times, indicating the presence of a {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja}} and possibly the provincial capital.<ref name="説明板">Shrine grounds information board.</ref>

The name "Iwa" may derive from the nearby shrine "In'yaku-sha," which enshrined the official seal and key of the provincial storehouse. A theory suggests "In" (seal) transformed into "I," and "Yaku" (key) became "Wa" through scribal errors.<ref name="説明板"/> Another theory posits that the shrine enshrines the deity {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi}}, known as Iwa Myōjin, brought from the {{ill|Iwa Shrine (Hyōgo)|en|伊和神社}} in {{ill|Harima Province|en|Harima Province}}.<ref name="説明板"/> The "Shinpū Tōki" (Edo period) mentions a local official, Satsuma-no-Kami, inviting Iwa Myōjin from Harima Province to create "Sōja Rokusha Daimyōjin," though this is considered a misinterpretation of earlier records.<ref name="地名">"Sōja Village" in ''Nagano Prefecture Place names''.</ref>

In the {{ill|Meiji period|en|Meiji period}}, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Village Shrine|en|村社}} under the modern shrine classification system and listed as a {{ill|Kensaihei Shrine|en|神饌幣帛料供進神社}}.<ref>Shrine stone monument.</ref>

== Sub-Shrines ==
* **Kokage Shrine** – Dedicated to silkworm cultivation, built during the height of the local silk industry.
* **Sōja Iwa Daimyōjin** – Five shrines representing:
** {{ill|Usui Sadamitsu|en|Usui Sadamitsu}}
** {{ill|Sakata no Kintoki|en|Sakata no Kintoki}}
** {{ill|Minamoto no Yorimitsu|en|Minamoto no Yorimitsu}}
** {{ill|Watanabe no Tsuna|en|Watanabe no Tsuna}}
** {{ill|Urabe no Suetake|en|Urabe no Suetake}}

=== Grounds ===
The shrine grounds feature numerous ancient {{ill|Zelkova serrata|en|ケヤキ}} trees. Two prominent zelkova trees at the entrance were formerly designated as a prefectural Natural Monument and are now protected as a city-level Natural Monument due to their age and declining health.<ref name="松本市">[http://takara.city.matsumoto.nagano.jp/city/158.html 伊和神社のケヤキ群] (Matsumoto City Cultural Property website).</ref>

'''Iwa Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|伊和神社}}, ''Iwa-jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Matsumoto, Nagano|en|松本市}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Nagano|af|Nagano-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Nagano|ar|ناغانو (محافظة)|arz|محافظه ناجانو|az|Naqano prefekturası|azb|ناقانو اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Nagano|be|Нагана (прэфектура)|bg|Нагано|bn|নাগানো প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Nagano|cdo|Nagano-gâing|ce|Нагано (префектура)|ceb|Nagano-ken|ckb|پارێزگای ناگانۆ|cs|Prefektura Nagano|cy|Nagano (talaith)|da|Nagano-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Nagano|eo|Gubernio Nagano|es|Prefectura de Nagano|et|Nagano prefektuur|eu|Nagano (prefektura)|fa|استان ناگانو|fi|Naganon prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Nagano|frr|Nagano (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Nagano|gl|Prefectura de Nagano|hak|Nagano-yen|he|נאגנו (מחוז)|hr|Nagano (prefektura)|hu|Nagano prefektúra|hy|Նագանո (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Nagano|ilo|Prepektura ti Nagano|it|Prefettura di Nagano|ja|長野県|ka|ნაგანოს პრეფექტურა|kaa|Nagano prefekturası|kn|ನಾಗನೊ (ಪ್ರಾಂತ್ಯ)|ko|나가노현|la|Naganoënsis|lt|Nagano prefektūra|lv|Nagano prefektūra|mk|Нагано (префектура)|mni|ꯅꯥꯒꯥꯅꯣ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|नागानो प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Nagano|ne|नगानो|nl|Nagano (prefectuur)|no|Nagano (prefektur)|nov|Nagano Prefekture|os|Нагано (префектурæ)|pam|Prepektura ning Nagano|pl|Prefektura Nagano|pnb|ضلع ناگانو|pt|Nagano|ro|Prefectura Nagano|ru|Нагано (префектура)|sco|Nagano Prefectur|se|Nagano prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Nagano|si|නගානො ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Nagano Prefecture|sk|Nagano (prefektúra)|sl|Prefektura Nagano|sr|Префектура Нагано|su|Nagano Prefecture|sv|Nagano prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Nagano|tg|Префектураи Нагано|th|จังหวัดนางาโนะ|tl|Prepektura ng Nagano|tr|Nagano (prefektörlük)|tt|Нагано (префектура)|uk|Нагано (префектура)|ur|ناگانو پریفیکچر|vi|Nagano|war|Nagano (prefektura)|wuu|长野县|zh|长野县|zh_classical|長野縣|zh_min_nan|Nagano-koān|zh_yue|長野縣|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}}, Japan. It is presumed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja}} of {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province}}. Its modern status is a former {{ill|Son-sha|en|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village Shrine}}. The official name is "Iwa-sha," but it is commonly referred to as "Iwa Shrine."<ref>[http://www.nagano-jinjacho.jp/shibu/syouenchiku.htm 松塩筑支部] (Nagano Prefecture Shrine Bureau).</ref> 

=== Deities ===
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)<ref>[http://www.genbu.net/data/sinano/iwa_title.htm 伊和神社] (Genbuko personal website).</ref>

=== History ===
In ancient times, {{ill|provincial governors|en|国司}} visited all shrines in their provinces, starting from the {{ill|Ichinomiya|en|Ichinomiya}}. To facilitate this, a {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja}} was established near the provincial capital to enshrine the gods collectively for easier rituals. Iwa Shrine is presumed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja}} of {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province}}. 

The provincial capital was initially located near {{ill|Ueda, Nagano|en|Ueda, Nagano}}, but it is believed to have moved to {{ill|Matsumoto, Nagano|en|Matsumoto, Nagano}} in the early Heian period.<ref>"Shinano Province" in {{Cite book|title=Nagano Prefecture Place names|editor=平凡社}}.</ref> The area around the shrine has been called "Sōja" since ancient times, indicating the presence of a {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja}} and possibly the provincial capital.<ref name="説明板">Shrine grounds information board.</ref>

The name "Iwa" may derive from the nearby shrine "In'yaku-sha," which enshrined the official seal and key of the provincial storehouse. A theory suggests "In" (seal) transformed into "I," and "Yaku" (key) became "Wa" through scribal errors.<ref name="説明板"/> Another theory posits that the shrine enshrines the deity {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi}}, known as Iwa Myōjin, brought from the {{ill|Iwa Shrine (Hyōgo)|en|伊和神社}} in {{ill|Harima Province|en|Harima Province}}.<ref name="説明板"/> The "Shinpū Tōki" (Edo period) mentions a local official, Satsuma-no-Kami, inviting Iwa Myōjin from Harima Province to create "Sōja Rokusha Daimyōjin," though this is considered a misinterpretation of earlier records.<ref name="地名">"Sōja Village" in ''Nagano Prefecture Place names''.</ref>

In the {{ill|Meiji period|en|Meiji period}}, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Son-sha|en|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village Shrine}} under the modern shrine classification system and listed as a {{ill|Kensaihei Shrine|en|神饌幣帛料供進神社}}.<ref>Shrine stone monument.</ref>

== Sub-Shrines ==
* **Kokage Shrine** – Dedicated to silkworm cultivation, built during the height of the local silk industry.
* **Sōja Iwa Daimyōjin** – Five shrines representing:
** {{ill|Usui Sadamitsu|en|Usui Sadamitsu}}
** {{ill|Sakata no Kintoki|en|Sakata no Kintoki}}
** {{ill|Minamoto no Yorimitsu|en|Minamoto no Yorimitsu}}
** {{ill|Watanabe no Tsuna|en|Watanabe no Tsuna}}
** {{ill|Urabe no Suetake|en|Urabe no Suetake}}

=== Grounds ===
The shrine grounds feature numerous ancient {{ill|Zelkova serrata|en|ケヤキ}} trees. Two prominent zelkova trees at the entrance were formerly designated as a prefectural Natural Monument and are now protected as a city-level Natural Monument due to their age and declining health.<ref name="松本市">[http://takara.city.matsumoto.nagano.jp/city/158.html 伊和神社のケヤキ群] (Matsumoto City Cultural Property website).</ref>
